climate.overview_html: The WMO State of the Climate update puts January-September 2026 at 1.47°C above pre-industrial, with records in sea level and ocean heat. At the COP31 leaders' summit, Guterres proposed a climate justice compact built on finance, fossil and deforestation roadmaps.

items.headline: WMO puts January-September 2026 at 1.47°C above pre-industrial
items.summary: The COP31 update says 2026 will rank among the four warmest years and sea level and ocean heat content are at records. The data end in September, before most El Niño effects; the full report is due March 2027.

items.headline: Guterres proposes a climate justice compact at the COP31 leaders' summit
items.summary: He called for roadmaps on $1.3 trillion in climate finance, transitioning from fossil fuels and ending deforestation. Lula said Brazil would draw up national roadmaps on fossil dependence and deforestation.

items.headline: World leaders arrive in Antalya as access problems keep delegates outside
items.summary: The leaders' summit opened with few heavyweight speakers, no US officials and the EU without new finance pledges.

major_events.name: Storm Charles and Bruna — Italy, Adriatic
major_events.status: Red alert in Tuscany; Adriatic next
major_events.impact: Italy's civil protection set a red alert for northwest Tuscany on Nov 12, orange for Liguria and Emilia-Romagna, yellow in nine more regions; up to 250-300 mm of rain is possible. Charles is merging with low Bruna, and MeteoNews puts the heaviest Adriatic totals near Rijeka and the Montenegro-Albania border.

major_events.name: Central Vietnam floods
major_events.status: Rain easing from Nov 12; rivers high
major_events.impact: Hue to Dak Lak saw 150-250 mm, locally over 400 mm. Flood warnings run from Hue to Khanh Hoa, reservoirs are releasing water and hundreds have been evacuated; a landslide hit the North-South Expressway in Dak Lak.

major_events.name: St. Johns River flooding — Florida
major_events.impact: Lake Harney stood at 9.1 ft (moderate) on Nov 11. Seminole County expects a crest of 9.7-10.3 ft and Sanford at 5.5-6 ft between Nov 20 and 23, with high water lasting into December.

major_events.name: South Africa heatwave and fire danger
major_events.impact: Heat has shifted to North West, Free State and southern Gauteng, with Upington forecast at 40°C. SAWS warns of extremely high fire danger in the Northern Cape, Free State and North West; thunderstorms hit the east.

major_events.name: Nor'easter and cold snap — eastern US
major_events.status: Rain on I-95, interior snow Nov 12-14
major_events.impact: 0.5-2 in. of rain and minor coastal flooding are possible Friday and Saturday, with 1-2 in. of wet snow in upstate NY and northern New England. The coldest air in about six months follows, with frost in the Carolinas and possible Deep South freezes Nov 14-15.

major_events.name: Bay of Bengal low
major_events.impact: IMD expects a depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal around Nov 15, with heavy rain on the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and gusts to 60 km/h. IMD has not forecast cyclone strength.

weather.overview_html: Storm Charles has merged with low Bruna and moved on to Italy, where Tuscany is on red alert for up to 300 mm of rain. Central Vietnam faces river flooding after more than 400 mm in places. In Florida the St. Johns River is now forecast to crest at Lake Harney around Nov 20-23, and the eastern US gets its first nor'easter and coldest air in six months.

items.headline: Italy issues red alert for Tuscany as Charles merges with low Bruna
items.summary: Northwest Tuscany, including Massa-Carrara and Lucca provinces, is on red alert for Thursday, with orange in Liguria and Emilia-Romagna. Forecasts allow for 250-300 mm of rain and gusts to 100 km/h.

items.headline: Portugal cancels more than 300 flights and shuts schools for Storm Charles
items.summary: Around 8,000 schools closed and 1,100 troops were placed on standby; Web Summit cancelled its second day. Mainland damage was limited after the storm passed.

items.headline: Flood warnings issued from Hue to Khanh Hoa after days of heavy rain
items.summary: Rain of 150-250 mm, locally over 400 mm, fell across central Vietnam. Reservoirs are releasing water and hundreds of residents have been evacuated; rain is forecast to ease from Nov 12.

items.headline: Seminole County expects St. Johns lakes to crest around Nov 20
items.summary: Officials call it a very prolonged slow flood. Lake Harney is forecast to reach 9.7-10.3 ft, and water is expected to stay high into December.

items.headline: South African heatwave spreads to several provinces with thunderstorms in the east
items.summary: Highs near 40°C are forecast in the Northern Cape; SAWS warns of extremely high fire danger across the interior until Friday.

items.headline: Nor'easter to bring first snow to interior New England, not a high-impact storm
items.summary: Rain totals of 0.5-2 in. are expected along I-95 with wet snow in the hills. CNN reports the following air mass will run 5-15°F below average.

items.headline: IMD expects a depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal around Nov 15
items.summary: Heavy rain is forecast for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, with 40-50 km/h winds gusting to 60 km/h over the Andaman Sea on Nov 14-15.

items.headline: Cempaka is typhoon No. 32 of 2026, the first year to reach that count since 1994
items.summary: The typhoon recurved south of Japan without landfall. By Nov 11 it was a Category 1 near 30N 154E, forecast to become extratropical.

renewables.overview_html: The EU cleared €2.04bn in aid to restart Belgium's 735 MW Princess Elisabeth tender. The US Senate voted 73-25 to advance a permitting bill that adds a federal backstop for interstate transmission. At COP31, five countries backed a goal of 300 million rooftop solar homes by 2030.

items.headline: EU approves €2.04bn aid to restart Belgium's first Princess Elisabeth Zone tender
items.summary: The 20-year scheme supports a wind farm of up to 735 MW and replaces a €682m scheme approved in 2024. The tender result is expected in Q4 2027.

items.headline: US Senate votes 73-25 to advance bipartisan permitting reform bill
items.summary: The bill adds a federal backstop for interstate lines of 230 kV and above and covers onshore and offshore wind. It still needs House passage.

items.headline: Five countries back COP31 goal to double rooftop solar homes to 300 million
items.summary: Australia, Bangladesh, Kenya, Nigeria and Vanuatu endorsed the Global Rooftop Solar Declaration on Energy Day, targeting 300 million homes by 2030 from about 150 million.

items.headline: 800 MW Vineyard Wind reaches full operation off Massachusetts
items.summary: The project came online hours after the 704 MW Revolution Wind reached full commercial operation on Nov 5. Together they add about 1.5 GW of US offshore wind.

items.headline: India approves INR 14,500 crore support for 92 GWh of grid storage
items.summary: The viability gap funding covers 60 GWh of pumped hydro, 30 GWh of batteries and 2 GWh of other technologies through FY2030-31, equal to 170% of existing grid storage. Batteries carry a 40% domestic-content rule.

science.overview_html: An arXiv study finds five AI weather models lose at most 1.4% RMSE when run in half precision, a direct cost lever for operational inference. A Nature Communications paper shows recent record heatwaves will be routinely exceeded under further warming, and GRL reports reef marine heatwaves intensify with depth.

items.headline: Half-precision inference costs AI weather models at most 1.4% in RMSE
items.summary: Aurora, Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet, SFNO and FastNet were run in fp16 versus fp32 on a single GPU, with global RMSE changing by at most 1.4%. Operators can cut inference cost and memory without retraining.

items.headline: Recent record heatwaves will be routinely exceeded under further warming
items.meta: Aglas-Leitner, Perkins-Kirkpatrick, Brunner et al. · Nature Communications
items.summary: The study compared 22 exceptional heatwaves from 2010-2023 with projections at 0-4.5°C of warming. A large share of future events exceed recent records in duration, cumulative heat and extent, especially late in the century.

items.headline: Marine heatwaves on coral reefs grow more intense with depth
items.meta: Yao et al. · Geophysical Research Letters
items.summary: Subsurface heatwaves in global reef regions occur on fewer days but reach higher intensity at depth, with day counts modulated by ENSO. The result weakens the idea of deeper reefs as thermal refuges.

items.headline: Weaker Southern Ocean carbon uptake helped fuel the early Eocene hothouse
items.summary: Lower biological carbon uptake in the Southern Ocean is linked to higher CO2 about 50 million years ago, amplifying an already warm climate.

items.headline: Sticky marine snow can carry six times more carbon to the deep ocean
items.summary: Particles with more gel-like material resist bacterial breakdown as they sink, delivering more than six times as much carbon to depth.

items.headline: Short-duration rain intensity rises about 20% even as totals fall
items.summary: Future simulations for an Israeli study area show lower total rainfall but peak short-duration intensity up about 20%, raising urban flood risk. Drainage design based on totals would underestimate it.

items.headline: 2026 Antarctic ozone hole ranks seventh-largest in 48 years
items.summary: NASA and NOAA put the peak at 27.1 million km² on Sept 18, driven by a strong polar vortex. Recovery remains on track for the 2070s.

items.title: Previsico and Mitigrate pair real-time flood forecasts with building-level risk data
items.body_html: UK flood-forecasting firm Previsico and Norwegian insurtech Mitigrate will combine hyperlocal flood prediction with vulnerability scores for underwriting, claims and loss prevention across the UK and Nordics. Mitigrate's platform covers more than 4 million Nordic and 3 million UK buildings, giving Previsico's forecasts a direct path into insurer workflows.

items.title: US Coast Guard ends 2026 Great Lakes trial of six Saildrone Voyagers
items.body_html: The six 33-ft USVs operated from April to November, collecting wind, wave, water-temperature and pressure data and tracking vessel traffic, before being pulled ahead of winter ice. They belong to 16 Voyagers under a $15.5M contract signed in March, and another test period is planned for spring 2027.

items.title: Galactic Energy's Ceres-2 returns to flight with ocean and commercial weather satellites
items.body_html: The rocket lifted off from Jiuquan and placed four satellites into a 535 km sun-synchronous orbit, recovering from its January debut failure. Payloads support ocean observation, commercial meteorology and space situational awareness, adding Chinese launch capacity for small observation satellites.
